causes.cause: No route, or no default gateway.

No DNS server set, or the wrong one.

title: Could not get lock (apt or dpkg)
match: Unable to acquire the dpkg frontend lock

causes.cause: Another apt or dpkg is running (often unattended-upgrades).
causes.fix: Wait for it to finish. Never delete the lock files.

causes.cause: Automatic updates are running.
A package install stopped halfway.

causes.cause: DNS can't resolve the mirror's name.
The kernel remounted it read-only after finding errors.
causes.fix: Plan a filesystem check (e2fsck) with it unmounted, and check the disk's health.

causes.cause: It is mounted read-only on purpose.
The disk is failing, or its connection is.
Check the disk's own health report.

The kernel killed a process to free memory. The log names it.
What uses memory now.
Memory and swap left.

title: A pod can't pull its image (ImagePullBackOff)

causes.cause: The image name or tag is wrong, or the registry doesn't have it. Events show the exact message.
The nodes can't reach the registry. Air-gapped, it must be an internal registry the nodes reach.
The registry needs a login and the pod has no pull secret.
The app exits on start; the reason is in the log of the run that crashed.
causes.fix: Step by step: la guide pod-not-running

causes.cause: It is killed for memory (Last State: OOMKilled) or by a failing liveness probe (Events).

title: A container was killed for using too much memory

causes.cause: Kubernetes: the container went over its memory limit (Last State: OOMKilled, exit code 137).
causes.fix: Raise the memory limit in its deployment, or find why it uses so much.

causes.cause: Docker: the container went over its memory limit, or the server ran out (oom=true).

title: A pod can't be placed on any node (Pending)

causes.cause: No node has enough free CPU or memory for the pod's requests, or none matches its node rules. Events name the reason.
Nodes are NotReady or cordoned (SchedulingDisabled).

title: kubectl's login was refused
match: You must be logged in to the server
the server has asked for the client to provide credentials

causes.cause: Your login token has expired: log in again the way your cluster gives logins (for VKS, the kubectl vsphere plugin).
kubectl is pointed at another cluster than you meant.

title: Your Kubernetes login may not do that

causes.cause: Your login has no permission for that, in that namespace.

title: kubectl can't reach the cluster
match: Unable to connect to the server

causes.cause: kubectl has no kubeconfig, or the wrong one (localhost:8080 means none).
The cluster's API address can't be reached from this server.
